stories.headline: Fed Holds Rates in Most Divided Vote Since 1992 as Inflation Concerns Rise

key_facts.fact: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% in an 8-4 vote, the most divided decision since October 6, 1992.
key_facts.excerpt: The 8-4 vote was the most divisive since October 6, 1992, and shows the breadth of opinion presumed incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will face

key_facts.fact: Three policymakers (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) voted against including an easing bias in the statement; a fourth dissented in favor of a rate cut.
key_facts.excerpt: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan... did not support inclusion of an easing bias in the statement

key_facts.fact: The Fed upgraded its inflation language from 'somewhat elevated' to 'elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices," the Fed said in its policy statement, a shift from previous language saying that inflation was just "somewhat elevated."

key_facts.fact: This was Jerome Powell's last policy press conference as Fed chair; his term ends on May 15, with Kevin Warsh as his presumed successor.
key_facts.excerpt: shows the breadth of opinion presumed incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will face in pursuing rate cuts that President Donald Trump says he expects from his chosen successor to Jerome Powell, whose term as central bank chief ends on May 15

key_facts.fact: Powell said the U.S. economy has been 'quite resilient' and is likely to keep growing above 2% this year due to solid consumer spending and data center investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said on Wednesday that the U.S. economy has been 'quite resilient' in the face of the Iran war energy shock, and is likely to keep growing at more than 2% this year because of solid consumer spending and data center investment.

key_facts.fact: Futures markets priced in little chance of a Fed rate cut by end of year; the March meeting minutes noted growing openness to a rate increase as the next move.
key_facts.excerpt: Futures markets were pricing in little chance of a Fed rate cut by the end of this year... The minutes of the Fed's March 17-18 meeting noted a growing number of policymakers were open to the idea that the central bank's next move might be a rate increase

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady in sharp divide over easing bias
US economy 'quite resilient', should keep growing above 2%, Fed's Powell says

stories.headline: Oil Surges to $126 Wartime High as Trump Lays Groundwork for Extended Iran Blockade

key_facts.fact: Brent crude briefly hit $126 per barrel on Thursday morning, a new wartime high, before falling back, as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude oil prices, the global benchmark, briefly hit a new wartime high of $126 per barrel Thursday morning before falling back down, as the critical Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed.

key_facts.fact: US gas prices jumped 7 cents to $4.30 per gallon, the highest since July 2022 and up 44% since the start of the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: US gas prices jumped another 7 cents to $4.30 for a gallon of regular, the biggest one-day jump in prices in the last six weeks. Gas is now at its highest price since July 2022... prices are up 44% since the start of war in Iran.

key_facts.fact: Trump told top advisers he wants the naval blockade of Iranian ports to continue and his team has begun laying groundwork for a longer-term closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump has told his top advisers in recent days he wants the US naval blockade of Iranian ports to continue... and his team has begun laying the groundwork for such an extension, including a longer-term closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: The US has spent $25 billion on the Iran war so far, according to a senior Pentagon official who told lawmakers Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: a senior Pentagon official told lawmakers Wednesday the US has spent $25 billion on the Iran war so far

key_facts.fact: Peace negotiations remain deadlocked; Pakistan could receive Iran's revised peace proposal by Friday, sources say.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan could receive Iran's revised peace proposal by Friday, sources say. Trump rejected a previous offer and peace talks appear deadlocked.

key_facts.fact: Iran's oil minister urged the public to cut fuel consumption, calling conservation a 'religious duty,' as the country's Supreme Leader said foreign actors have no place in the Persian Gulf.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad urged the public to cut consumption, calling 'conservation and saving' a general principle 'and a religious duty,' as he dismissed the impact of the US naval blockade.

sources.title: Live updates: Oil surges to new wartime high as Trump mulls extended blockade of Iranian ports
Trump sees blockade extension as best option for forcing Iran back to the negotiating table

stories.headline: US Sanctions 35 Iran-Linked Entities, Warns Chinese Refiners Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury sanctioned 35 entities and individuals for their roles in Iran's shadow banking sector, which facilitated tens of billions of dollars in sanctions evasion.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Government ratcheted up pressure on Tehran on Tuesday (April 28, 2026), imposing sanctions on 35 entities and individuals for their roles in Iran's shadow banking sector

key_facts.fact: Treasury warned financial institutions they face sanctions risk over dealings with Chinese teapot refineries in Shandong province that process Iranian oil.
key_facts.excerpt: The Treasury urged financial institutions in a statement to avoid facilitating transactions involving independent refineries, known as 'teapots,' that import Iranian oil, as such transactions may expose them to sanctions.

key_facts.fact: China purchases approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports, with teapot refineries accounting for the majority of these imports.
key_facts.excerpt: China purchases approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports, the Treasury noted, with teapot refineries accounting for the majority of these imports.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's Kharg Island export terminal is 'soon nearing storage capacity,' which could force Tehran to cut production and lose $170 million in daily revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Bessent said Iran's main export terminal on Kharg Island is 'soon nearing storage capacity,' which could force Tehran to cut production and lose about $170 million in daily revenue.

key_facts.fact: The moves come less than a month before Trump's planned visit to Beijing, adding another irritant to US-China relations.
key_facts.excerpt: The move risks adding yet another irritant for China ahead of an expected summit between US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping next month.

sources.title: U.S. warns banks of sanctions risk over China 'teapot' refineries handling Iranian oil
U.S. imposes sanctions on 35 individuals, entities for aiding Iran's sanctions evasions
US warns of sanctions risks for Chinese refiners of Iranian oil

stories.headline: US and 5 Latin American Nations Condemn China's Retaliation Over Panama Canal Ports

key_facts.fact: Bolivia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, and the US released a joint statement criticizing China's 'targeted economic pressure' on Panamanian-flagged ships.
key_facts.excerpt: Bolivia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, and the United States have released a joint statement in support of Panama, while criticising Chinese economic retaliation

key_facts.fact: China detained nearly 70 Panamanian-flagged ships in March, far exceeding historical norms, according to the US Federal Maritime Commission.
key_facts.excerpt: China detained nearly 70 Panamanian-flagged ships in March, according to the US Federal Maritime Commission, a number 'far exceeding historical norms'.

key_facts.fact: The retaliation followed Panama's Supreme Court annulling contracts that allowed CK Hutchison's subsidiary to administer the Balboa and Cristobal port terminals.
key_facts.excerpt: Panama's Supreme Court in late January annulled contracts that had allowed a subsidiary of Hong Kong's CK Hutchison to administer the Balboa and Cristobal port terminals

key_facts.fact: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was 'deeply concerned' by China's economic pressure, calling it a threat to sovereignty.
key_facts.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said separately on X that Washington was 'deeply concerned' by China's economic pressure on Panama. 'We stand in solidarity with Panama. Any attempts to undermine Panama's sovereignty are a threat to us all,' he said.

key_facts.fact: China also retaliated against Maersk and MSC, whose subsidiaries were granted contracts to replace CK Hutchison; COSCO suspended operations at the Balboa terminal.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese shipping giant COSCO has suspended operations at the Balboa terminal... Representatives of Maersk and MSC were both summoned by China's Ministry of Transport for 'high-level discussions'

sources.title: US, Latin America countries criticise China's retaliation over Panama Canal

stories.headline: Samsung Q1 Operating Profit Surges 756% to Record ~$38.5B, Warns Memory Shortage Deepens

key_facts.fact: Samsung reported Q1 revenue up 69% YoY to approximately $90.2B and operating profit up 756% to approximately $38.5B, both above estimates, driven by AI memory demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics reported an over eightfold increase in first-quarter operating profits on Thursday, hitting a new record

key_facts.fact: DRAM average selling prices rose roughly 90-95% sequentially from Q4 to Q1, signaling sharp tightening in AI-driven memory markets.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics reported DRAM ASPs rising roughly 90-95% sequentially from Q4 to Q1, signaling a sharp tightening in memory markets tied to AI-driven demand.

key_facts.fact: Samsung warned the memory shortage will worsen in 2027 as customers are already placing orders for that year, leading to a projected supply gap larger than 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung warns memory shortage to deepen next year as 2027 orders come in

key_facts.fact: Next-generation HBM4E samples are set to be delivered in Q2, and Samsung expects double-digit revenue and earnings growth in its foundry business in Q2.
key_facts.excerpt: Next-gen HBM4E samples to be delivered in Q2... Expects double digit revenue and earnings growth Q2 earnings to improve on higher HBM4 base-die shipments

sources.title: Samsung Q1 earnings: AI memory chip demand drives record profit
Samsung warns memory shortage to deepen next year as 2027 orders come in

stories.headline: SpaceX Falcon Heavy Returns After 18-Month Gap, Launches ViaSat-3 F3 Satellite

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy lifted off at 10:13 a.m. EDT on April 29 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A, its first flight since October 2024's Europa Clipper mission.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's most powerful operational rocket, the Falcon Heavy, lifted off Wednesday carrying a massive communications satellite on its 12th flight since 2018.

key_facts.fact: The mission carried ViaSat-3 F3, a 6.6-ton broadband satellite designed to deliver over 1 Tbps of throughput to the Asia-Pacific region, completing Viasat's three-satellite constellation.
key_facts.excerpt: At roughly 6.6 tons, it is a high-capacity broadband communications satellite designed to deliver more than 1 terabit per second of throughput across the APAC region once on station.

key_facts.fact: Both side boosters successfully landed at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, while the center core was expended.
key_facts.excerpt: the center core was expended, while the two side boosters returned to Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Both boosters executed successful landings—one at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40) and the other at Landing Zone 2 (LZ-2).

key_facts.fact: Viasat confirmed initial signal acquisition minutes after satellite separation, confirming the spacecraft is healthy in orbit; service entry is expected by late summer 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellite successfully separated from the launch vehicle's upper stage just under five hours after liftoff, with initial signals acquired minutes later, confirming the satellite is healthy in orbit

key_facts.fact: Several additional Falcon Heavy missions are planned for 2026, including the Griffin lunar lander for Artemis and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's launch marks the return of Falcon Heavy to the active manifest and points to a busy year ahead. Several additional missions are planned for 2026, including the Griffin lunar lander, which is part of the Artemis program, and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

sources.title: SpaceX launches 6-ton ViaSat-3 F3 satellite on Falcon Heavy rocket
Viasat Confirms Successful Launch and Initial Signal Acquisition of ViaSat-3 F3

stories.headline: France Unveils Plan to Phase Out Coal by 2030, Oil by 2045, Gas by 2050

key_facts.fact: France announced a 'first of its kind' roadmap to phase out coal by 2030, oil by 2045, and gas for energy purposes by 2050, presented at the Santa Marta fossil fuel transition conference in Colombia.
key_facts.excerpt: France announced a 'first of its kind' plan to phase out coal by 2030, oil by 2045 and gas by 2050 on Tuesday, April 28, during a global conference aimed at breaking reliance on fossil fuels.

key_facts.fact: The roadmap consolidates existing French climate targets under one umbrella; analysts said no other country had published such a clear and comprehensive fossil fuel exit plan.
key_facts.excerpt: France's roadmap does not present new pledges but brings existing climate and energy policies and targets under one umbrella with an explicit goal. Analysts said no other country had published such a clear and comprehensive plan

key_facts.fact: Nearly 60 nations attended the Santa Marta conference, co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, including EU members, fossil fuel producers Canada and Norway, and developing oil giants Angola and Nigeria.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 60 nations were in attendance, from the European Union and major fossil fuel producers Canada and Norway, to developing oil giants Angola and Nigeria and small island developing states like Tuvalu.

key_facts.fact: France generates only a fraction of its electricity from hydrocarbons thanks to nuclear power; the roadmap also commits to phasing out fossil fuel production and electrifying heating and transport.
key_facts.excerpt: France only generates a fraction of its electricity from hydrocarbons, thanks to its extensive nuclear power generation... the roadmap also committed to phasing out fossil fuel production, electrifying sectors like heating and transport

key_facts.fact: The conference took place amid soaring fuel prices from the Iran war; France pushed ahead after a proposal for a global fossil fuel roadmap was blocked at the COP30 summit in November.
key_facts.excerpt: The conference takes place against a backdrop of soaring fuel prices and a global supply crunch stemming from the Iran war... France had decided to push ahead on its own after a proposal for a global fossil fuel roadmap was blocked at the COP30 climate summit in November.

sources.title: France unveils plan to ditch all fossil fuels by 2050
